episodes.159467: A funnel cloud was sighted near Galveston Island.
episodes.159520: Some marine thunderstorm winds were observed.
episodes.159530: Afternoon thunderstorms that developed along the sea breeze produced several wind gusts along the Brevard and Indian River County coasts.
episodes.159609: An upper level disturbance crossed into West Virginia on August 3rd, which set the stage for scattered showers and thunderstorms that afternoon. Some thunderstorms grew strong enough to inflict damaging wind gusts and resulted in downed trees in Roane, Jackson, and Putnam Counties. ||Heavy downpours associated with the afternoon and evening storms also resulted in localized flooding issues in Putnam County. Local weather stations observed between two to three inches of rainfall had fallen in the county that evening. State Route 34 was closed near the Arby's in Teays Valley that night in both directions due to high water.
episodes.159716: High pressure began to reposition over the Great Basin, cutting off the stream of deep monsoonal moisture over the region. Even so, enough moisture lingered over the area which resulted in another round of diurnal showers and thunderstorms. The stronger storms produced heavy rain which led to localized flash flooding and debris flows in San Miguel, Gunnison and Eagle counties.
episodes.159772: Afternoon storms produce strong marine wind gusts along West Central and Southwest Florida coast.
episodes.161406: Flash flooding occurred as a stalled front and weak low pressure interacted in a tropical air-mass to generate showers and thunderstorms with heavy rainfall.
episodes.162009: An environment marked by warm and moist conditions favored strong to severe thunderstorms while an outflow boundary collided with a sea breeze circulation under mid-level energy traversing across the region.
episodes.162084: Scattered thunderstorms developed and move south across southeast Arizona from Tucson eastward during the afternoon and evening.  Damaging wind gusts and flash flooding occurred with storms in eastern Pima County, mainly in east Tucson.
episodes.162410: A persistent rainy pattern across the southeastern big bend brought rainfall amounts in excess of foot during the first 12 days of the month to portions of southeastern Taylor, southern Lafayette, and Dixie counties. This rainfall fell on already saturated grounds and resulted in significant, long duration areal flooding. In addition, significant river flooding occurred across the Steinhatchee River basin. The Steinhatchee River crested at its 2nd highest crest on record at 24.6 ft on August 7th, which is well into the moderate flood category. Many roads were closed, and many homes were impacted. The river remained in at least minor flood stage for 20 days.
episodes.162439: Slow moving thunderstorms developed over the mountains, as the monsoon plume remained in place on this day. With the heavy rain that stemmed from these thunderstorms along with high antecedent soil moistures from rainfall over the past several days, the flash flood threat remained high with a few reports of flash flooding noted near the higher terrain.
episodes.162467: Moist south to southwest wind flow associated with a mid-level trough over the eastern U.S. contributed to an active day of showers and thunderstorms across South Florida.
episodes.162829: Waterspouts were observed near the coast.

A persistent rainy pattern across southeastern Taylor county brought rainfall amounts in excess of foot during the first 12 days of the month. This rainfall fell on already saturated grounds and resulted in significant, long duration areal flooding. In addition, significant river flooding occurred across the Steinhatchee River basin.  The Steinhatchee River crested at its 2nd highest crest on record at 24.6 ft on August 7th, which is well into the moderate flood category.  Many roads were closed, and many homes were impacted.  The river remained in at least minor flood stage for 20 days.  Damage cost was estimated.

Several trees and power lines were blown down near the town of Eleanor. One tree fell onto a home located on Eleanor Circle.
In the town of Eleanor, one tree was uprooted.
Heavy rain in the Cimarrons produced intermittent flash flooding and a debris flow of rocks and branches on National Forest Service Road 861.1 (Middle Fork Road), near the Owl Creek Pass junction.
